title: Chemistry — Mission 1: The Unlabeled Samples
description: Three unlabeled samples turned up in the prep room. Use periodic trends and bonding theory to figure out what they are before the shipment gets returned.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Believes every mystery sample is a teaching opportunity.

priya.name: Priya
priya.description: Just wants the shelves labeled correctly before inventory day.

periodic_table.name: Periodic Table Card
periodic_table.description: Groups, periods, and trends at a glance.

conductivity_probe.name: Conductivity Probe
conductivity_probe.description: Tells you whether a dissolved sample carries current.

elements.text: Three samples, no labels, and the supplier wants an answer by Friday. Good news: their properties tell the whole story if you know what to look for.
I just need to know which shelf each one goes on. Metal, nonmetal, or metalloid.

elements.prompt: Mika hands you the periodic table card.

options.text: "Let's check each sample's position on the table and its trends before touching anything."
"Shiny ones are metals, that's usually close enough."

elements.text: With the card in hand, let's confirm you can read the trends correctly.
No card yet — let's fix that before this goes any further.

config.question: Moving left to right across a period, atomic radius generally:

options.text: Increases, because more protons pull electrons in
Decreases, because increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer
Stays the same across a period
Increases only for metals, decreases only for nonmetals

config.explanation: Increasing nuclear charge across a period pulls the electron cloud in tighter, shrinking atomic radius.

config.prompt: Order these elements from most metallic to most nonmetallic character: Sulfur, Sodium, Silicon.

config.question: Sample C dissolves in water and the solution conducts electricity strongly. What kind of bonding does Sample C most likely have?

options.text: Ionic — it dissociates into freely moving ions
Covalent — molecules stay intact in solution
Metallic — a sea of delocalized electrons
No bonding — it's a pure element

config.explanation: Strong conductivity in solution points to an ionic compound dissociating into mobile ions.

elements.text: Metal, metalloid, ionic compound — labeled and shelved correctly. Inventory day is saved.
They're labeled, but next time let's check the trends before we guess.

elements.prompt: The samples are shelved. What now?

options.text: Walk Priya through how the periodic table predicted every property before you tested anything.
Shelve them and move on. Good enough for today.

elements.text: So the table isn't just a chart to memorize — it actually predicts how things behave. That's going to save me a lot of guessing.

ending.title: Trend Reader
ending.description: Classified every sample from periodic trends and bonding behavior alone, and taught Priya to do the same.

ending.title: Shelves Labeled
ending.description: The samples are sorted and shelved. The deeper trend-reading lesson can wait.
